name: Subcutaneous
descriptionSimple: An injection into the layer of fat just under the skin.
descriptionPractitioner: Injection into subcutaneous tissue. Absorption is generally slower than intravenous and varies with site, depth, formulation and injected volume.
generalLimitations: Statements about this route describe the route itself. Whether any specific compound has been studied or reported by this route is recorded per compound, with its own source.

name: Intramuscular
descriptionPractitioner: Injection into skeletal muscle. Absorption varies with site, muscle perfusion and formulation.
generalLimitations: Route-level description only. Compound-specific evidence is recorded separately.

name: Intravenous
descriptionPractitioner: Direct delivery into the circulation, bypassing absorption. Used in controlled clinical settings.
generalLimitations: Route-level description only. Compound-specific evidence is recorded separately.

name: Intranasal
descriptionSimple: Delivery into the nose, usually as a spray or drops.
descriptionPractitioner: Delivery across the nasal mucosa. Bioavailability is highly molecule- and formulation-specific and cannot be generalised across peptides.
generalLimitations: Nasal absorption of one peptide says nothing about another. Every intranasal record on this site names its compound, formulation, population and source.

name: Oral
descriptionPractitioner: Gastrointestinal delivery. Most peptides are subject to enzymatic degradation and poor permeability; oral viability depends on the specific molecule and formulation technology used.
generalLimitations: There is no general statement that peptides can be taken orally. Oral evidence is recorded per compound and per formulation.

name: Sublingual / Buccal
descriptionSimple: Held under the tongue or against the inside of the cheek.
descriptionPractitioner: Delivery across oral mucosa. Absorption depends on molecular size, lipophilicity, formulation and contact time.
generalLimitations: Route-level description only. Compound-specific evidence is recorded separately.

name: Topical
descriptionPractitioner: Application to skin or mucosa. A topical effect at the application site is a different claim from systemic absorption.
generalLimitations: Local activity does not establish systemic exposure, and systemic exposure does not follow from topical application.

name: Intradermal
descriptionSimple: An injection into the skin itself rather than beneath it.
generalLimitations: Route-level description only. Compound-specific evidence is recorded separately.

name: Intra-articular
descriptionSimple: An injection into a joint space.
descriptionPractitioner: Injection into a joint cavity, performed in a clinical setting.
generalLimitations: Route-level description only. Compound-specific evidence is recorded separately.

name: Other / Specialised
descriptionSimple: A route that does not fit the common categories.
descriptionPractitioner: Specialised or investigational delivery routes. The specific route is described on the record itself.
generalLimitations: Always read the compound-specific record; this category groups routes that differ materially from one another.
